h: Throwing a Ninja Party in Chelmsford
p: Parties are one of the big reasons families book here, and it's easy to see why. Nobody needs to know the rules, everyone gets a go, and the kids burn off so much energy that the sugar rush from the cake barely registers. If you're planning one, book well ahead, as weekend party slots are popular, and check the age guidance so the whole group fits the session.

Keep the guest list realistic, and ask what's included before you invite anyone. Having a couple of extra adults on hand to help with shoes, socks and coats makes the start of the party far less chaotic.

Chelmsford itself has a fair bit to fill the rest of the day. Chelmsford Museum, in Oaklands Park, is a good, free stop for local history. The riverside paths along the Chelmer and Blackwater Navigation make a pleasant walk towards the countryside, and Danbury Country Park, a few miles east, has lakes and woodland for a breath of fresh air. Garden fans can visit RHS Garden Hyde Hall near Rettendon, which is lovely in every season.
Wherever you head afterwards, plan for a proper feed. Hanging off things for an hour makes everyone ravenous.
